threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Rust DOCX comparison, editing, revision-resolution, validation, scrubbing and PDF/PNG rendering engine, exposed through the native CLI, PyO3 Python library/CLI, wasm-bindgen Node/browser APIs and an optional Python MCP server over stdio. Document bytes flow through package admission, OPC/XML processing and operation-specific logic into returned bytes, text or host-owned output files. Legacy DOC conversion is a separate OLE parser. The Rust library forbids unsafe code. The normal runtime is a caller-owned process, not a repository-provided multitenant web service. Separately privileged workflows publish releases and packages and run external Jules review/remediation actions. Evidence: README.md:13-41; src/lib.rs:86-165; src/legacy_doc.rs:13-50; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381; .github/workflows/release.yml:230-369; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:254-324.
assets: Confidential document text, revisions, comments, images, embedded package parts and generated DOCX/PDF/PNG/diff/report bytes. Text-returning MCP tools intentionally disclose selected document content to the connected host; exported binary outputs are stored under the granted root. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-218; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:234-255.

Integrity of input files, existing outputs, edit plans and source-to-edit correspondence. Legacy plans conditionally verify source_sha256; this is not unconditional authentication or authorization. Evidence: src/edit.rs:2081-2089; src/publication.rs:168-173.

Process memory, CPU and availability while processing hostile ZIP, XML, OLE, font, raster-image and layout inputs. Default package budgets are 64 MiB compressed/per-part, 256 MiB inflated, 10000 entries and depth 256; comparison defaults instead permit 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB inflated. Evidence: src/admission.rs:39-100; src/legacy_doc.rs:5-11; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:77-96.

Filesystem authority: native CLI ambient output paths; Python/Node host filesystem operations; MCP's separately granted, persistent directory capability; native Markdown image resource root; native renderer's installed/user font directories. These authorities are independently enforced and are not interchangeable. Evidence: src/publication.rs:146-225; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2876; src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111.

Installed executable integrity and publication authority. Current self-update trusts HTTPS release assets plus same-release SHA-256 checksums; its compiled release-key list is empty and first-signed-release threshold is None. Release signing secret, GitHub publication token, local registry credentials, Jules API key and Codecov token are distinct sensitive capabilities. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48; src/update.rs:198-257; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-309; .github/workflows/release.yml:356-369; scripts/release.sh:918-919; scripts/release.sh:935-956; scripts/release.sh:1069; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:28-50; .github/workflows/ci.yml:102-107.
trustBoundaries: Untrusted DOCX bytes -> package admission -> OPC/XML engine: admission checks archive budgets, duplicate/case-folded names, allowed compression, encryption, structural ZIP defects, bounded inflated streams and XML policy. Normal archive opens reject zip_defects; debug intentionally uses the unchecked opener to inspect rejected packages. These are in-memory package names, not filesystem extraction destinations. Evidence: src/admission.rs:439-574; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51; docs/FILESYSTEM_PUBLICATION.md:9-12.

Unchecked public XML -> DOM: permissive parse_xdocument explicitly does not enforce input policy. Callers must first admit package/XML or use checked APIs. Checked XML policy rejects DTD/custom entities and applies depth/tag/attribute limits; no blanket safety claim extends to raw permissive APIs. Evidence: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:19-36; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-65; src/wml_document.rs:50-55.

Edit plan and document -> prepared result: schema and nonempty author checks, optional exact source SHA-256 guard, package restrictions and operation/anchor validation precede returned results. Preview and application are engine operations; publishing is separately host-owned. No user identity or human approval is established by an author string or source digest. Evidence: src/edit.rs:1740-1761; src/edit.rs:2074-2100; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:170-217.

MCP client arguments -> root-confined document I/O: operator chooses --root, default cwd; build_server resolves it and opens native _OutputRoot once. Python containment is an early diagnostic; actual reads and publication use capability-relative operations. MCP tool hints inform hosts but do not implement per-user authorization or write approval. All connected callers share the configured root authority; overwrite is a caller-supplied option. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-108; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199; docs/adoption/mcp.md:39-41.

MCP edit/render -> root-relative outputs: docx_edit writes out_dir/clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff, report.json and optional redline.pdf/redline-page-NN.png; docx_render writes out_dir/page-NN.png and optional render.pdf. Publisher stages all members first but commits per file, so later commit failures can leave earlier committed members. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-218; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:234-255; src/publication.rs:115-130; src/publication.rs:168-173.

Native CLI -> ambient output paths: explicitly requested paths use publication::publish_paths, holding parent capabilities and staging bytes before commit. This intentionally does not impose MCP root confinement. Python and Node CLI wrappers own their I/O and use direct host writes; sharing the Rust parser does not share the native publisher. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:203-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:1002-1026; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-79; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111.

Native Markdown image targets -> local resource files: explicit resource_path overrides the Markdown parent directory, with '.' for a bare filename. image_loader canonicalizes that root, rejects inappropriate decoded targets and reads through a held OutputRoot capability. Hosted callers must separately decide what input authority to grant. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2840-2876; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2936-2943; docs/FILESYSTEM_PUBLICATION.md:78-81.

Native rendering -> host fonts: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides platform defaults; otherwise macOS uses HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Windows APPDATA/jubarte/fonts, and other platforms XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts. macOS discovery also searches system/Word font paths and HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>; family must be one normal path component. These reads use renderer/OS authority, not MCP document-root authority. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2194-2216; src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236; src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652.

Operator self-update -> GitHub release -> executable replacement: explicit command, platform selection, version decision and optional confirmation precede delegated installation; SHA256SUMS.txt is configured and the extracted binary must be a regular file. Current compiled keys require no signature. Windows selects a ZIP archive, other published targets use tar.gz; extraction/swap internals belong to self_update and were not independently inspected in this pass. Evidence: src/update.rs:44-48; src/update.rs:186-257; src/update.rs:299-321; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-41.

Tag/release infrastructure -> public executable assets: v* tag push triggers the release workflow, which checks tag/manifests, builds with read permissions, and grants contents:write only to the release job. ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY is scoped to the signing step, decoded into RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.XXXXXX/keyN and cleaned on exit; missing secret fails only when committed public keys exist. The GitHub token separately authorizes gh release create for github.repository with dist/* and notes.md. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-55; .github/workflows/release.yml:230-309; .github/workflows/release.yml:356-369.

Local release operator -> registry publication: release.sh obtains typed tag confirmation unless YES is set, pushes the release tag, separately publishes crates.io and two npm packages, and sends dist/pypi/* to PyPI using UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN. These registry/account capabilities are distinct from GitHub release signing and publication. Evidence: scripts/release.sh:875-901; scripts/release.sh:918-919; scripts/release.sh:935-956; scripts/release.sh:1042-1069.

PR/repository content -> CI runner and external review: CI/docs execute repository-controlled build/generation code on self-hosted runners with contents:read and nonpersisted checkout credentials; runner filesystem/network isolation is not established by token permissions. Jules review separately receives JULES_API_KEY and a token with PR/check write capability; same-repository/non-Dependabot guards apply. Companion remediation additionally gates session startup to TRUSTED_USERS and configured events, but delegates AUTO_CREATE_PR with require_plan_approval:false to a pinned external action whose implementation is absent here. Evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-48; .github/workflows/docs.yml:76-99; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-52; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:254-324.

CLI plan staging has separate implementations: native write_plan uses exclusive publication; Python and Node wrappers construct PID-based partial paths and open them with ordinary truncating writes before rename. A lower-trust local actor requires shared-directory entry rights and permissive OS symlink handling to influence this boundary. Evidence: src/edit/record.rs:142-165; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:403-414; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:409-427.
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier can control ZIP/XML/OPC, legacy OLE, embedded image/font and Markdown data processed by a caller. This alone does not grant process execution, ambient filesystem paths, trusted environment variables or publication credentials.

An MCP caller can supply tool arguments and edit plans and request reads/writes within the configured root, including overwrite=true. Additional host approval is a host policy; MCP annotations are not enforcement. Authority outside the granted document root must be assessed separately from root-confined document operations.

A local CLI caller already has the invoking account's ambient file authority. Demonstrating arbitrary paths supplied by that caller is not itself a privilege gain; a meaningful violation needs an untrusted document-driven path or another actor with less authority.

A PR author controls proposed source/build inputs. Same-repository PRs and trusted-author remediation have materially different gates from fork PRs. Access to self-hosted runner resources depends on runner configuration and workflow admission that are not present in this source.

An attacker controlling only unsigned release assets and their accompanying checksums is outside checksum-corruption protection; changing those assets is not assumed without a separate GitHub/release compromise prerequisite. Current shipped updater signing is disabled by explicit empty compiled keys.

External-action internals, remote Jules/GitHub authorization, registry account protection, host filesystem ACLs, process resource limits and browser embedding policy are not established by this architecture review.
securityObjectives: Reject malformed or over-budget untrusted packages before expensive engine processing, while retaining checked XML policy at raw-input boundaries. Comparison's larger limits and any caller overrides must remain explicit. Evidence: src/admission.rs:63-108; src/admission.rs:439-574.

Preserve source/edit correspondence when a source digest is supplied and refuse invalid plans before producing publishable edits. Keep author attribution separate from authentication. Evidence: src/edit.rs:1740-1761; src/edit.rs:2074-2100.

Confine MCP document reads, parent creation and publication to the held root capability; reject unsafe export names and output symlinks; preserve no-overwrite behavior under publication races. Evidence: src/publication.rs:146-199; src/publication.rs:228-273; docs/FILESYSTEM_PUBLICATION.md:60-69.

Keep output durability and atomicity claims aligned with implementation: native per-file staging/commit differs from multi-file transactions, directory bundles and direct-write wrapper paths; Windows directory synchronization has a documented limitation. Evidence: src/publication.rs:115-130; src/publication.rs:168-173; docs/FILESYSTEM_PUBLICATION.md:28-58; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111.

Do not turn document relationships or Markdown resource targets into unrestricted host/network access. Explicit resource roots and caller-provided loaders are capabilities, not document authority. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2876; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2936-2943; src/document_comparer.rs:100-107.

Protect executable/package publication credentials, bind released artifacts to selected versions and targets, and describe current checksum-only updater trust accurately. Evidence: src/update.rs:44-48; src/update.rs:198-257; .github/workflows/release.yml:41-49; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-309; scripts/release.sh:870-899.

findings.title: Converting a small legacy DOC can exhaust memory through reused text pieces
findings.summary: An attacker-supplied DOC can reuse one physical text range across thousands of contiguous logical pieces. `legacy_doc::read` decodes every declared character into an unbounded vector, allowing megabyte-sized input to request billions of characters and exhaust the converting process.

severity.rationale: Availability impact is limited to the converting process. Processing attacker-controlled documents is supported and the amplification requires no privileged configuration; shared-service exposure is not assumed. SECURITY.md recommends external memory/CPU isolation.
severity.changeConditions: A decoded-output budget would remove this path; shared service exposure without worker isolation would increase impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent static trace confirms attacker-controlled counts and reusable physical offsets reach unbounded allocation; no runtime reproduction was performed.

codeEvidence.explanation: Caller-controlled legacy bytes enter read before DOCX generation.

codeEvidence.label: legacy-read
codeEvidence.explanation: read forwards document FIB length and parsed pieces to main_text without a decoded-text budget.

codeEvidence.label: legacy-count
codeEvidence.explanation: ccp_text is read directly from the FIB.

codeEvidence.explanation: Every piece independently retains physical fc, including reused ranges.

codeEvidence.explanation: Contiguous CP coverage does not cap aggregate decoded output.

codeEvidence.label: legacy-loop

codeEvidence.label: legacy-push
codeEvidence.explanation: Every decoded character grows the StoryChar vector.

codeEvidence.label: legacy-cli
codeEvidence.explanation: CLI converts legacy bytes before DOCX admission.

rootCause.summary: `doc_to_docx` calls `read`, which reads `ccp_text` and physical piece offsets from untrusted streams. `main_text` checks contiguous increasing CP coverage and physical byte access, but permits repeated physical ranges and never bounds total decoded characters before appending `StoryChar` values.

findings.remediation: Enforce a configurable aggregate decoded-character/byte budget before main_text iterates and return a typed LEGACY_DOC refusal on excess; preserve legitimate overlapping physical ranges within budget.

counterEvidence: OLE chains are bounded by file sectors (src/legacy_doc.rs:681-704,765-803); this limits physical streams, not logical piece expansion.
Decreasing CPs, gaps and out-of-range bytes are rejected (1154-1204), but none rejects repeated physical fc values.
limitations: Static validation only; no malicious input or app execution.
validation.summary: Confirmed direct public/CLI reachability and lack of aggregate decoded-text budget. Two thousand contiguous million-character pieces can reuse the same million physical bytes while requesting two billion StoryChar entries; all logical CPs fit u32 and all physical reads remain in bounds.

dataflow.summary: DOC FIB and Clx -> pieces -> main_text per-CP loop -> Vec<StoryChar>::push
dataflow.outcome: Memory/CPU exhaustion and possible process termination

likelihood.why: Document-controlled lengths directly drive unbounded allocation.

reachability.summary: Document suppliers can trigger this when users or applications call public legacy conversion or CLI convert on their DOC; no operator privileges or remote deployment are assumed.

attackPath.summary: Supply a readable legacy DOC with a large FIB story length and repeated physical text ranges under contiguous increasing CPs, then request conversion.

remediationTests: Construct a small repeated-range piece table and assert refusal before large allocation.
Accept legitimate reused ranges when decoded length remains below budget.

findings.title: Unbounded HTML colspan expands a tiny altChunk into gigabytes of generated XML
findings.summary:
An internal HTML chunk containing
x
causes one billion generated gridCol elements, approximately 20 GB of XML, from a tiny input. This can exhaust memory and terminate the conversion process or embedding host. No remote service exposure is assumed.

severity.rationale: A tiny document attribute deterministically drives multi-gigabyte allocation in supported rendering APIs. Impact is converting-process availability, with no remote service assumed. External process quotas recommended by SECURITY.md can contain impact.
severity.changeConditions: Enforced logical-column and generated-output budgets remove this path; an exposed shared renderer without isolated workers increases impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent source trace independently verifies the attribute parser, generated-column loop, and placement after admission. No runtime exploit was executed.

codeEvidence.label: html-entry
codeEvidence.explanation: Public PDF conversion accepts caller-controlled DOCX bytes.

codeEvidence.label: html-layout
codeEvidence.explanation: PDF with_pages enters the common with_layout pipeline.

codeEvidence.label: html-expansion
codeEvidence.explanation: Admission checks original bytes before relationship-targeted HTML expansion; generated XML is parsed afterward.

codeEvidence.label: html-chunk
codeEvidence.explanation: Relationship bytes are decoded to HTML then passed to html_to_wml.

codeEvidence.label: html-span
codeEvidence.explanation: colspan becomes any positive usize with no upper bound.

codeEvidence.label: html-columns
codeEvidence.explanation: Sum of spans controls an unbounded generated gridCol loop before DOM construction.

rootCause.summary: The public renderer admits the original ZIP, then `altchunk::expand` loads relationship bytes, converts HTML/MHT, and calls `html_to_wml`. `Builder::start` accepts unrestricted positive `usize` spans. `end_table` sums them and serializes one `gridCol` per logical column into a growing string. Original archive and XML budgets therefore do not bound this generated representation.

findings.remediation: Apply a documented maximum colspan and total logical table-column count, use checked addition, and enforce a shared generated-output budget during HTML conversion and repeated altChunk expansion. Refuse over-budget conversion before allocating the expanded XML.

counterEvidence: Package admission restricts compressed and inflated source bytes and XML depth.
HTML text and font names are XML-escaped, and scripts are skipped.
SECURITY.md explicitly requires caller process memory/CPU limits; these can contain the blast radius but do not bound or reject this expansion.
This conclusion is from source inspection; no application code or reproduction was executed.
limitations: No crafted package or application code executed.
validation.summary: Confirmed a one-cell table with colspan=1000000000 selects a billion-iteration serialization loop, even though the source table is only dozens of bytes. The check occurs after source admission and before any generated XML parse. The value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.

dataflow.summary: DOCX relationship -> altchunk::expand -> HTML colspan -> cell.span -> sum of spans -> gridCol serialization

likelihood.why: A small input directly controls the number of generated XML elements.

reachability.summary: Attacker controls a document submitted to a public conversion API or CLI user. No privileged configuration, external relationship or live deployment is required.
reachability.attacker: A caller supplying a crafted DOCX to the public PDF, PNG, or render-report API.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX with an internal HTML altChunk containing an enormous numeric colspan, then request PDF/PNG rendering or a layout report.

remediationTests: Assert oversized colspan and excessive aggregate table columns return a typed error before generating the grid.
Test repeated references to the same chunk against an aggregate generated-output budget.

findings.title: Renaming referenced XML parts bypasses depth checks and can crash document processing
findings.summary: A DOCX can name its referenced header, footer, footnotes or endnotes part with a non-.xml suffix such as .dat. Admission treats it as opaque bytes, while rendering or comparison follows the relationship and recursively parses it as XML without limits. Deeply nested content can exhaust the stack and terminate the host process.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can bypass the declared XML depth gate on normal conversion/comparison paths and cause process availability loss. No remote exposure is assumed; CPU/memory worker isolation limits collateral damage.
severity.changeConditions: Mandatory policy checks at every XML-consuming boundary would close the path; a shared service without process isolation would increase impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent traced suffix classification, arbitrary relationship target loading, comparison/render consumers and recursive DOM calls. Conversion investigator independently confirmed no consumer recheck. No runtime stack-overflow test was executed.

codeEvidence.label: xml-recursion
codeEvidence.explanation: The permissive parser recurses for every nested element without a depth gate.

rootCause.summary: `admit` selects XML-policy validation by filename suffix, with a special case only for the main part. OPC relationships can identify auxiliary XML with arbitrary names. `load_chrome_part` and `pre_process_markup` retrieve those bytes and use `parse_xdocument`, whose recursive `parse_element` assumes an earlier depth check. This mismatch lets attacker-controlled auxiliary XML skip that check entirely.

findings.remediation: Apply the active XML limits to every relationship/content-type-identified XML part before DOM construction, independent of filename suffix. Prefer checked per-consumer APIs with the admitted limits, including headers, footers, notes and other auxiliary XML.

counterEvidence: All .xml/.rels entries and an arbitrarily named main part are checked; the omission concerns auxiliary targets.
PartFs bounds inflation and checks OPC metadata attributes but stores other part bytes without XML-depth checks (src/opc/mod.rs:348-377).
The raw permissive parser is documented as unchecked; the vulnerability is its use after incomplete package admission, not mere public availability of that API.
Default and comparison limits both specify XML depth 256 (src/admission.rs:71,94).
limitations: No crafted package executed; exact crashing depth is platform/stack dependent.
Related auxiliary consumers share the admission failure; no claim that every parser consumer was exhaustively audited.
validation.summary: Confirmed arbitrary auxiliary names survive PartFs loading (src/opc/mod.rs:348-377) and strict translation (src/strict_translation.rs:810-826). Normal render headers/footers and nonidentical comparison notes reach unchecked parsing. A nested .dat XML part can remain far below the 64 MiB per-part limit while exceeding the depth-256 policy by orders of magnitude.

dataflow.summary: DOCX part name -> is_xml=false -> byte-budget-only admission -> relationship target -> part_string -> permissive DOM recursion
dataflow.source: Untrusted auxiliary XML bytes and relationship target

likelihood.why: Normal relationship consumers trust admission but receive unchecked deeply nested bytes.

reachability.summary: A document supplier controls internal part names and relationships. Public render/comparison calls accept package bytes; no privileged settings or network access are needed.
preconditions: Use a non-.xml/.rels auxiliary target with matching content-type metadata.
For comparison, use nonidentical input documents so preprocessing runs.

attackPath.summary: Create an otherwise admitted DOCX with a header or notes relationship pointing to a deeply nested XML part named .dat; request rendering, or compare it with a nonidentical document.

remediationTests: Rename deeply nested headers/footnotes to .dat with valid internal relationships and assert typed XML-depth refusal for render and compare.
Verify custom-named valid auxiliary XML remains supported and active caller limits are preserved.

originalCandidate.title: Auxiliary part names can bypass XML admission

Auxiliary header/footer/notes/styles targets can have arbitrary extensions. header word/header.dat referenced from document.xml sectPr and rels: with_layout admits then opens package (src/convert/mod.rs:771-781), load_chrome_part follows rid and reads arbitrary path (20768-20782), chrome_part_xml calls permissive recursive parse_xdocument without limits (20795-20797), which recursively calls parse_element (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:655-657). Deep header.dat can pass admission then stack-overflow renderer. Same notes path pre_process_markup src/document_comparer.rs:4737-4751 reaches DOM after compare admission.

extensions.corroboration: Conversion investigator returned src/convert/mod.rs:20768-20797 and 21285-21298 with no revalidation found.

findings.title: WMF payload reads cross record boundaries and repeatedly retain subsequent records as text
findings.summary: A placeable WMF with nonzero bounds and repeated 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT records, each declaring size=7 words, count=65535, and options=0, causes each record with sufficient trailing data to retain roughly 64 KiB of subsequent records as text. About 1 MiB of such records can generate more than 4 GB of retained strings before layout. The sibling geometry operations also permit overlapping repeated processing. This can exhaust memory or monopolize conversion CPU.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can amplify a bounded embedded WMF into gigabytes of retained text or repeated geometry work on a normal rendering path. Availability is affected; reads stay inside the allocated file buffer, so memory disclosure or memory corruption is not established. External process limits contain collateral impact.
severity.changeConditions: Enforced record-local payload bounds close the demonstrated amplification; shared unisolated rendering would increase impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently checked record size handling, text counts/slices, allocation, retained outputs and image relationship reachability. No reproduction was executed.

taxonomy.category: Record-boundary validation failure causing resource amplification

codeEvidence.explanation: The sibling EMF helper restricts point spans to each record end.

rootCause.summary: Document image relationships feed `decode_image`, which invokes `metafile::render` and `raster_wmf`. Each WMF record size is checked against remaining file bytes, but its payload readers still see the whole file. `EXTTEXTOUT` and `TEXTOUT` read a declared string beyond the record, allocate it in `wmf_text`, and retain it; the outer loop advances by the smaller record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline operations repeat the same missing record-boundary check.

findings.remediation: Construct a slice for each complete WMF record and perform every fixed-field, string, font, ring, and point read relative to that slice. Reject records whose declared counts exceed their payload using checked arithmetic. Add aggregate decoded-text and operation budgets as defense in depth.

counterEvidence: WMF/EMF raster dimensions are capped at 384 pixels per side, and line/polygon painting clips coordinates to the canvas.
Checked multiplication prevents WMF record-size overflow on wasm32.
The sibling EMF read_emf_points helper checks point reads against off + size; that control is absent from the affected WMF operations.
Input admission and image crate decoder limits do not inspect or constrain these internal WMF text allocations.
Caller process resource limits can contain availability impact. No runtime reproduction was executed.
limitations: No malicious WMF or DOCX was run.
Impact is availability; no out-of-buffer memory read or code execution is claimed.
validation.summary: Confirmed a 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record (size=7 words, count=65535, options=0) can read 65535 following bytes while advancing 14 bytes, repeatedly retaining overlapping strings. Nonzero placeable bounds satisfy wmf_text; repeated record bytes contain non-whitespace so strings are kept. Record-local EMF bounds do not protect WMF.

findings.title: Nested legacy DOC field results cause quadratic conversion work
findings.summary: A legacy DOC containing repeated field-begin/separator pairs makes `Story::blocks` rescan an increasingly long stack of false field states for every next character. Hundreds of kilobytes of field markers can require tens of billions of state checks, monopolizing conversion CPU independently of text-piece expansion.

severity.rationale: The attacker supplies a normal supported parser input and causes disproportionate CPU use. Impact is availability of the converting process; no remote service or elevated authority is assumed. External CPU quotas can terminate the workload.
severity.changeConditions: Constant-time field-code tracking or a small enforced nesting cap removes quadratic behavior; shared unisolated service deployment would increase impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent confirms field markers survive decoding and no field-depth guard precedes the per-character .any scan. Complexity follows directly from the stack transitions; no timing reproduction was run.

taxonomy.category: Quadratic work from unbounded field-state rescanning

codeEvidence.label: field-public
codeEvidence.explanation: Public conversion calls read on untrusted DOC bytes.

codeEvidence.label: field-decode
codeEvidence.explanation: read decodes FIB and piece-table text to StoryChar, including field control markers.

codeEvidence.label: field-blocks-call
codeEvidence.explanation: Decoded attacker-controlled characters enter Story::blocks.

codeEvidence.label: field-stack
codeEvidence.explanation: Every character scans the complete field-state stack before pushing, separating or popping a field.

rootCause.summary: `read` decodes legacy field markers and calls `Story::blocks`. The block parser keeps all nested field states in `fields` and computes `fields.iter().any(...)` for each character. A begin marker pushes true; its separator changes that state to false without popping it. Repeating begin/separator pairs leaves an ever-growing false prefix, so later scans visit all prior levels. No nesting/work budget or cached active-code count bounds the resulting quadratic work.

findings.remediation: Track the number of active field-code frames incrementally so in_code is constant time, and enforce a documented nesting/work budget before growing fields; retain correct nested field-result semantics.

counterEvidence: CP/offset checks and OLE chain budgets constrain physical input traversal but not Story::blocks field nesting.
Simple nested field behavior is tested (src/legacy_doc.rs:1946 onward), but the control has no depth/work cap.
The scan short-circuits on true; the demonstrated separated-result stack is all false and defeats that short circuit.
limitations: No benchmark, malicious input or application execution was performed.
validation.summary: After N begin/separator pairs the stack contains N false entries. Processing successive pairs examines prefixes of length 0..N, totaling Theta(N^2) boolean checks; N closing field markers can also scan decreasing false prefixes. A single physical text piece is sufficient, so bounding repeated physical ranges does not remediate this separate complexity failure.

dataflow.summary: DOC text control bytes -> main_text -> StoryChar -> Story::blocks -> repeated fields.iter().any

likelihood.why: Short repeated control-byte sequences create the worst-case stack state.

reachability.summary: A document supplier controls the marker sequence processed by public legacy conversion and CLI convert. No large declared story, repeated physical ranges or privileged settings are required.

attackPath.summary: Supply a readable DOC story with many nested field-begin markers immediately followed by separators, then invoke legacy conversion.

remediationTests: Use a deterministic work counter on separated nested fields and assert linear processing as depth increases.
Test nested code/result transitions and an explicit excessive-depth refusal without wall-clock assertions.

originalCandidate.title: Legacy DOC field-state quadratic scan
originalCandidate.originalEvidence: Story::blocks src/legacy_doc.rs:1595-1617 computes fields.iter().any(|&code| code) for every StoryChar, using an unbounded Vec<bool> stack. N repetitions of U+0013 (field begin), U+0014 (separator) leave N false entries; each next begin/separator scans every false ancestor, causing quadratic work on ~2N source bytes. N end markers also scan/pop. Single 1MiB piece can encode ~500k field levels and ~250 billion checks. Distinct from memory expansion; candidate CWE-407.

findings.title: Recording a plan in a shared directory can overwrite unrelated files
findings.summary: Python and Node CLI plan recording writes to a predictable `.<plan>.<pid>.partial` path using truncating, symlink-following file APIs. A different local user who can create entries in the plan directory can pre-place that path as a symlink to an unrelated file writable by the victim, causing that file to be overwritten with plan JSON before the later rename.

severity.rationale: The path crosses from a directory-entry creator's authority into the victim account's writable files, but requires a shared writable plan directory, predictable/observable process ID, and a filesystem policy permitting symlink following. Private plan directories avoid this attack, and some OS policies block cross-user symlinks. No remote attack or demonstrated deployment is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Exclusive private staging removes the issue; evidence of routine privileged execution in attacker-writable directories would raise impact/likelihood.

confidence.rationale: Source directly establishes deterministic temporary names and nonexclusive symlink-following writes in both wrappers; the external shared-directory prerequisite is explicit and no runtime exploit was executed.

taxonomy.category: Unsafe temporary-file creation following symbolic links

rootCause.summary: Both CLI dispatchers route recording requests through validation/preview, then derive a staging filename from the resolved plan basename and current PID. Node `fs.writeFileSync` and Python `Path.write_bytes` open that name with default truncating writes, rather than exclusively creating a private staging file. A preexisting symlink is therefore followed before `renameSync`/`os.replace` can install the plan. Plan validation does not authorize the link's unrelated referent.

findings.remediation: Use exclusive randomized private staging in the resolved destination directory, write through the newly created descriptor, and atomically replace the plan. Apply the native publisher's approach to both Python and Node wrappers; reject preexisting staging paths rather than following them.

counterEvidence: The attacker needs directory-entry creation rights and a predictable or observable PID; this is a conditional local attack.
Resolving the plan target is intentional supported behavior, but does not safely open the separately derived staging path.
Private directories and OS symlink restrictions can prevent exploitation.
The native CLI uses the safer publisher; this finding covers Python and Node wrappers.
limitations: No symlink exploit or application code was executed.
No default shared-directory or privileged-use deployment is asserted.
validation.method: Parent static source trace and sibling comparison
validation.summary: Confirmed --plan plus operation flags reaches these sinks for valid non-dry-run recordings; neither path checks or exclusively creates the partial. Corruption occurs at the first write, so later rename failure or cleanup does not undo it. Native write_plan instead uses publication::publish_paths and its exclusive random staging directory.
